hook.text: How do scientists compare the warming power of CO₂ to methane to aerosols? They use radiative forcing.

buildup.text: Radiative forcing measures the change in energy balance at the top of the atmosphere, in watts per square meter.

discovery.text: Positive forcing warms the planet (greenhouse gases); negative forcing cools it (aerosols, some clouds).

twist.text: Human-made aerosols have masked some warming—cleaning up air pollution could actually accelerate heating.

climax.text: Total anthropogenic forcing is about +2.7 W/m²—with CO₂ contributing roughly two-thirds of that figure.

punchline.text: Forcing is the scoreboard—and it keeps climbing.

quiz.question: What does a positive radiative forcing indicate?
